answer: Order-book capacity decays to zero each epoch unless an agent re-buys a routing slot at a public forge. The forge auctions slots by burning ember, and its clearing rule tracks bidder counterparties: when $k$ accounts settle over half their volume through the same liquidity pool, the $k$-th linked account must burn $20 \cdot 2^{k-1}$ ember to activate one ferrous of trade bandwidth. A solo newcomer burns 20 ember per ferrous each epoch, while one operator routing $n$ clones through a shared pool must burn $20(2^n - 1)$ ember every epoch or capitalize $n$ isolated pools.
